title: Blood transfusion
summary: The hospital blood bank from a licensed source to the bedside - sources, units received, the storage log, requests with the transfusion consent, compatibility tests, issue, the two-person bedside check within 30 minutes, observations, the end, reactions with their incident, discards and returns - and the registers and measures the PHC asks for.
workflow: MSDS Category I 21-25 and 104; II A 82-86; II B and II C 62-65; the II C manual p154-163 (decisions 43)
markdown:
# Blood transfusion

| Source | What the surveyor checks | Haspataal |
|---|---|---|
| Cat I 21 (PDF p42-43), II C 62 (p154) | Written SOPs for the whole blood chain, followed; traceability at every step | Every step recorded and linked: `GET /blood/units/{unit_id}` is one unit's chain; the SOPs themselves are the hospital's |
| Cat I 22 (p43-44), II C 63 (p157-158) | The service under the Punjab Blood Transfusion Safety Act 2016: a PBTA licence, or an MOU with a licensed blood establishment; only legal blood reaches patients; temporary storage | `/blood/sources` with the PBTA licence and the MOU from the compliance register; units only from active sources; the storage log |
| Cat I 23 (p44), II C 64 (p159-160) | Informed consent of every recipient (signed, or the physician's note in an emergency) | A request is refused without the patient's Given transfusion consent of the stay (`BLOOD_CONSENT_REQUIRED`, database rule) |
| Cat I 25 (p45-46), II C 65 (p161-163) | Reactions recorded, analysed, actions; the Authority informed (the Act s.13) | `POST /blood/transfusions/{id}/reaction` (Table 11's fields) creates the incident; `POST /blood/reactions/{id}/recheck` adds the regrouping and the Authority's notice |
| Cat I 104 (p117) | The percentage of transfusion reactions, of wastage and of component usage, and the turnaround of issue, before the CQI committee | `GET /blood/statistics`, `GET /blood/statistics/pdf` |

A hospital that also runs its own blood *center* (donors, screening, collection, components: owner decision B1,
decisions 48) uses the separate service `blood_center` ([Blood center](blood-center.md)); its components reach this
blood bank only by their release, as units of the source kind `OwnBloodCenter`, each with its `donation_number`. The
ABO compatibility of a unit is the laboratory's test result; Haspataal records it and shows both groups, and enforces
no compatibility matrix of its own.

The service `blood_transfusion` (it requires inpatient care) is switched on in the facility settings
([Facility profile and services](facility-profile-and-services.md)) once an active licensed source, someone who may
test and issue (`blood.bank.operate`) and someone who may transfuse (`blood.transfuse`) exist. New requests and units
received are refused while it is not Active (`CAPABILITY_INACTIVE`); while it is Retiring, the requests made before
continue to their end.

Who: the **Lab Admin** keeps the sources (`blood.bank.manage`); **lab technicians and verifiers** receive units
(`blood.receive`), test, issue and keep the log (`blood.bank.operate`); **doctors** request (`blood.request`); **ward,
OT and ER nurses and doctors** transfuse (`blood.transfuse`); the **Quality Officer**, the **Owner** and the clinical
staff read (`blood.view`).

## 1. The sources and the service (Lab Admin, Hospital Admin)

1. `POST /blood/sources` with an `Idempotency-Key`: `name`, `kind` (`BloodCenter` | `HospitalBloodBank`; the hospital's
   own center is `OwnBloodCenter`, see [Blood center](blood-center.md)),
   `licence_number` (PBTA), optionally `agreement_document_id` (the MOU or contract from
   `GET /facility/compliance-documents`). A II B or II C hospital without its own blood bank transfuses under such a
   contract (II C p158). `BLOOD_SOURCE_EXISTS`.
2. `GET /blood/sources`; `PATCH /blood/sources/{source_id}` with `expected_version` (`is_active` false stops receiving).
3. `POST /establishment/changes/preview` then `POST /establishment/changes` with `blood_transfusion` → `Active`; the
   preview lists `CAPABILITY_PREREQUISITE` (`blood_source`, `blood_bank_staff`, `transfusion_staff`) until they exist.

## 2. The blood bank (lab technician)

4. `POST /blood/units` with an `Idempotency-Key`: the bag as labelled: `source_id`, `unit_number`, `component`
   (`WholeBlood` | `RedCells` | `FreshFrozenPlasma` | `Cryoprecipitate` | `Platelets`), `abo`, `rh`, `expires_at`,
   `screened` (true, never pre-ticked), optional `volume_ml`, `collected_on`, `arrival_temperature_c`.
   `BLOOD_UNIT_EXISTS`, `BLOOD_UNIT_EXPIRED`, `CAPABILITY_INACTIVE`.
5. `GET /blood/units`: the stock (on the shelf, reserved, out), soonest expiry first; `expired` true: discard it.
6. `POST /blood/storage-checks` with an `Idempotency-Key`: `equipment`, `storage_kind` (`BloodRefrigerator` +2 to +6 C,
   `PlasmaFreezer` at most -30 C, `PlateletIncubator` +20 to +24 C: the II C manual p155; settings
   `blood_refrigerator_min_c` ... may change them), `temperature_c`, `alarm_working`; out of range needs
   `action_taken` (`STORAGE_CHECK_ACTION_REQUIRED`) and emits `blood.storage.out_of_range`. `GET /blood/storage-checks`,
   `GET /blood/storage-checks/pdf`.
7. `GET /blood/requests`: the worklist (open requests, Emergency first); `blood.request.created` refreshes it.
   `GET /blood/requests/{request_id}`.
8. `POST /blood/requests/{request_id}/crossmatches` with an `Idempotency-Key`: `unit_id` (on the shelf, the component
   requested), the patient's `patient_abo` / `patient_rh` on this sample, `sample_taken_at`, `method`, `result`
   (`Compatible` reserves the unit for the request). `BLOOD_UNIT_STATE`, `BLOOD_UNIT_EXPIRED`, `VALIDATION_ERROR`.
9. `POST /blood/requests/{request_id}/issue` with an `Idempotency-Key`: `unit_id`, `crossmatch_id` (only an Emergency
   request with `uncrossmatched_note` may leave it out: `BLOOD_CROSSMATCH_REQUIRED`), and the collecting nurse or
   doctor signs for the unit on the bank's screen: `collector_username`, `collector_password` (`STEP_UP_REQUIRED`;
   `ADMINISTRATION_NOT_AUTHORIZED` when not a registered nurse or doctor). The answer's `start_by` is 30 minutes
   after the issue. Emits `blood.unit.issued` to the ward.
10. A unit coming back: `POST /blood/transfusions/{transfusion_id}/return`: `fit_for_use` true within 30 minutes (signed
    back into the refrigerator; it keeps its reservation; `BLOOD_UNIT_OUT_TOO_LONG` after), or false with
    `discard_reason` and `note` (not given, discarded).
11. Out of the stock: `POST /blood/units/{unit_id}/discard` (`reason`, `note`: the wastage measure) or
    `POST /blood/units/{unit_id}/return-to-source` (`note`: the contract's take-back).
12. When the request is done: `POST /blood/requests/{request_id}/close` (the units still reserved go back on the shelf).

## 3. The request (doctor)

13. `GET /consents?patient_id=...`: the patient's transfusion consent of this stay must be `Given` (signed, or the
    doctor's emergency note: [consent](consent.md)); none: take it first.
14. `POST /blood/requests` with an `Idempotency-Key`: `admission_id` or `er_visit_id`, optional `booking_id`, `component`,
    `units_requested`, `urgency`, `indication`, `consent_id`; for `Emergency` only, optionally `uncrossmatched_note`.
    `BLOOD_CONSENT_REQUIRED`, `PRESCRIBER_NOT_AUTHORIZED`, `VALIDATION_ERROR` (not a current stay), `CAPABILITY_INACTIVE`.
    The request is for the stay the doctor has open: its `admission_id`, or the emergency visit's `er_visit_id`;
    `booking_id` only when the blood is for an operation of that stay. The consent picked (`GET /consents?patient_id=`)
    belongs to the same stay.
15. Follow it with `GET /blood/requests/{request_id}`; `POST /blood/requests/{request_id}/cancel` with why, only before
    any blood was given (`BLOOD_REQUEST_STATE`); `POST /blood/requests/{request_id}/close` when done.

## 4. At the bedside (nurse; ward, theatre or emergency)

16. On `blood.unit.issued`: `GET /blood/transfusions/{transfusion_id}`; show the countdown to `start_by`.
17. `POST /blood/transfusions/{transfusion_id}/observations` with an `Idempotency-Key`: the baseline before the start,
    then as taken (`temperature_c`, `pulse`, `bp_systolic`, `bp_diastolic`, `respiratory_rate`, `note`).
18. `POST /blood/transfusions/{transfusion_id}/start`: `wristband_code` (or `identity_check` TwoIdentifiers;
    EmergencyOverride with `identity_note`; `GET /wristbands/verify` checks a band first), the five `checks` (`identity`,
    `unit_number`, `expiry`, `product`, `bag`: every one true, none pre-ticked; a failure is
    `BLOOD_BEDSIDE_CHECK_FAILED`: record the unit as not given, step 10), and the second nurse or doctor's
    `second_checker_username` / `_password` (`STEP_UP_REQUIRED`, `DUAL_CONTROL_SAME_PERSON`). `BLOOD_UNIT_OUT_TOO_LONG`
    after 30 minutes. `BLOOD_CONSENT_REQUIRED`: the patient withdrew the transfusion consent since the request (the bank's
    issue is refused the same way): do not transfuse; record the unit as not given or sign it back (step 10).
    On `blood.consent.withdrawn` (critical: the patient withdrew the consent) the requests in `cancelled_requests` are
    already cancelled; for every unit in `units_out` show "Do not start: consent withdrawn" and, for a transfusion
    running, "Stop the transfusion" (`POST /blood/transfusions/{transfusion_id}/end` with `outcome` Stopped).
19. `POST /blood/transfusions/{transfusion_id}/end`: `outcome` Completed, or Stopped with `end_note`; optional
    `volume_given_ml`. `ended_late` is true more than 4 hours after the issue (II C p157).
20. A reaction: `POST /blood/transfusions/{transfusion_id}/reaction` with an `Idempotency-Key`: `noticed_at`,
    `reaction_type`, `reaction_class` (Haemolytic, Anaphylactic, DelayedHaemolytic with `delayed_after` and optional
    `antibody`, Bacterial with `organism`, Other: the II A manual's form, Table 11), `fatal` (only with `harm` Death),
    `signs`, `action_taken`, optional `possible_reason`, `harm`, `wrong_blood` (the sentinel event).
    The incident is created in the same call (its number is in `reaction_report.incident_number`); its review and
    actions follow [incidents and sentinel events](incidents-and-sentinel-events.md). Emits `blood.reaction.reported`.
    `BLOOD_REACTION_EXISTS`.

## 5. Registers and monitoring (Quality Officer, blood bank in charge)

21. `GET /blood/reactions/{reaction_id}/pdf`: the reaction on the II A manual's report form (Table 11) for the blood
    bank and the file; haemolytic and life-threatening reactions go to the blood bank within 10 days, fatal ones by
    telephone the next working day, then in writing.
    `POST /blood/reactions/{reaction_id}/recheck` (`blood.bank.manage`): `recipient_group_recheck`,
    `donor_group_recheck`, and `authority_informed_at` with `authority_reference`; each once (`BLOOD_REACTION_RECORDED`).
22. `GET /blood/statistics?date_from=&date_to=` and `GET /blood/statistics/pdf`: the four measures of indicator 104.
23. `GET /blood/registers/transfusions/pdf` and `GET /blood/registers/reactions/pdf` (Table 11): each patient printed is
    logged as a read of their record. The inspection pack carries the same four documents (`blood_*`).
24. `GET /blood/units/{unit_id}`: one unit's whole chain, from the source to the patient (traceability).

## 6. Retiring the service

The preview of `blood_transfusion` → `Retired` lists the open work: open requests (close or cancel them), units in the
bank (use, return to the source or discard them) and units out on a ward (finish or sign back). The registers and the
history stay readable afterwards; a reaction's incident stays in the incident register.
